subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should OpenClaw own Slack OAuth token rotation natively in the Slack plugin, and what storage/config/runtime contract should it use for client secrets and single-use refresh tokens?
rationale: The request is security-motivated and aligned with Slack's OAuth flow, but the proposed config shape, secret storage, live token adoption, setup UX, retry behavior, and compatibility story are product/security choices rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Implement plugin-owned native rotation
options.body: Build the feature in the Slack plugin with a maintainer-approved secret/state contract, status/doctor recovery, docs, and upgrade tests while leaving existing static-token setups unchanged.

options.title: Keep external rotation documented
options.body: Document the external daemon/SIGUSR1 workaround and keep OpenClaw's Slack credential model static until maintainers approve owning refresh-token custody.

options.title: Wait for a generic credential-rotation seam
options.body: Defer Slack-specific implementation until OpenClaw has a shared plugin API for rotating OAuth credentials across channels/providers.

recommendation.title: Implement plugin-owned native rotation
recommendation.body: Build the feature in the Slack plugin with a maintainer-approved secret/state contract, status/doctor recovery, docs, and upgrade tests while leaving existing static-token setups unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Slack auth/security work and the security/product nature of secret custody make this the best available routing candidate from the observed history.
